transcript: Good morning. Today is a day to call your friend. Having social relationships can make us happy.

Research links adult friendship, social connection, and quality conversations with well-being. Calling a friend can reduce loneliness and improve mood, though face-to-face contact generally has the strongest benefit.
Here's a fresh idea from a recent podcast, Scientific American. Match friendship style to your friend: talk over coffee or do an activity together. Face-to-face contact best maintains friendships.
Your action for today: call a friend and suggest a short in-person activity. Have a great day.
Good morning. Today is a day to plan your time. With an ever-hectic schedule, sometimes it's easy to forget to schedule something else that's crucial to your well-being: time off.
Scheduling rest is not a luxury; recovery time helps reduce fatigue and supports well-being and performance.
Here's a fresh idea from a recent podcast, WorkLifePsych. Treat rest as a scheduled need, not a reward. List activities that genuinely restore you and add one small recovery block to your week.
Your action for today: block 30 minutes of non-work rest on your calendar. Have a great day.
Good morning. Today is a day to be a hugger today. The average hug lasts 2.1 seconds but for the endorphins to transfer it needs to last seven seconds or longer.
Hugs can reduce stress and support bonding, but benefits depend on consent and comfort. A 5, 10 second hug is a reasonable, evidence-informed suggestion rather than a strict seven-second rule.
Here's a fresh idea from a recent study. Try a consensual, comfortable hug lasting about five to ten seconds. It is the duration researchers found most beneficial for reducing stress and anxiety.
Your action for today: ask a friend for a five-to-ten-second hug. Have a great day.
Good morning. Today is a day to take the stairs. Taking the stairs can release endorphins that boost your mood and reduce stress, leading to increased happiness.
Short stair climbing can improve mood and energy immediately; repeated short bouts may reduce perceived stress.
Here's a fresh idea from a recent study. Three 30-second stair-climbing bouts daily for six weeks reduced perceived stress in inactive young adults.
Your action for today: schedule three short stair climbs this week. Have a great day.
Good morning. Today is a day to use everybody's name. Always use person name before talking or making point - it is the best compliment for people.
Using someone's name can signal that you value their individuality and help build rapport, but it works best when used naturally and respectfully.
Here's a fresh idea from a recent study. Hearing your own name activates attention and identity-related brain regions. Use it occasionally before a key message.
Your action for today: try: "Sam, here's the one thing I need.". Have a great day.
Good morning. Today is a day to have less social media. Spend less time on electronic friends and more time with real flesh and blood ones.
For ages 16, 25, research links in-person friendships more strongly with wellbeing and health than online friendships, while reducing social-media use can modestly improve wellbeing.
Here's a fresh idea from a recent study. Reduce social-media use by at least 30 minutes a day for two weeks. Use the freed time to meet or call a friend in person.
Your action for today: set a 30-minute daily social-media limit and plan one face-to-face chat. Have a great day.
Good morning. Today is a day to smile! We smile because we're happy, and smiling causes the brain to release dopamine, which makes us happier.
Smiling can make people feel a little happier, but it is not a cure for depression or a proven dopamine-release mechanism.
Here's a fresh idea from a recent article. A single voluntary smile can briefly lift mood, but repeated or pressured smiling can backfire. Try one genuine smile when something small feels good.
Your action for today: university of Florida. Have a great day.

Good morning. Today is a day to be grateful. You might try starting each day by acknowledging one thing you're grateful for. You can do this while you're brushing your teeth or just waiting for that snoozed alarm to go off.
A brief daily gratitude practice can support well-being; pairing it with an existing routine such as brushing teeth helps make it easier to repeat.

Here's a fresh idea from a recent study. Write down one thing you appreciate each morning or evening. The study found links with lower stress, anxiety, tiredness, and loneliness lasting up to six days.
Your action for today: write one specific gratitude before brushing your teeth today. Have a great day.
Good morning. Today is a day to give a compliment. Giving a sincere compliment is a quick, easy way to brighten someone's day while giving your own happiness a boost.
Research finds people underestimate how much compliments uplift others and overestimate how awkward they seem. Giving a genuine compliment can improve both people's mood.
Here's a fresh idea from a recent podcast, The Science of Happiness. Offer a brief, genuine compliment to someone you don't know well. Small kind gestures can create connection and lift your mood.
Your action for today: compliment someone's outfit or choice today. Have a great day.
Good morning. Today is a day to plan your day. Sit down at the end of the day and make a basic list for the following day.
Planning tomorrow at the end of the day can improve next-day focus and performance, especially when you list and prioritize a few concrete tasks.

Here's a fresh idea from a recent study. Each evening, choose no more than three concrete tasks for tomorrow and keep them visible. A four-week study found this improved completion, focus, and motivation.
Your action for today: write three specific tasks for tomorrow before bed. Have a great day.

Good morning. Today's card comes from the legends set. Here's a line often attributed to Andy Rooney: Everyone wants to live on top of the mountain, but all the happiness and growth occurs while you're climbing it.
Andy Rooney was a CBS 60 Minutes commentator and writer, but this mountain-climbing line is a misattribution.
Here's a fresh idea from a recent article. Treat progress and effort as the reward, not just the final achievement. Notice what makes you feel alive during the process.
Your action for today: do one small task that challenges you and enjoy the effort. Have a great day.

Good morning. Today's card comes from the legends set. Here's a line often attributed to Oprah Winfrey: You are responsible for your life. You can't keep blaming somebody else for your dysfunction. Life is really about moving on!
Oprah Winfrey is a media executive, producer, and philanthropist known for her talk show and advocacy for education and girls' leadership.
Here's a fresh idea from a recent article. Pause before blaming, then name your own role and pick one solution.
Your action for today: ask: "What can I do differently today?". Have a great day.
Good morning. Today's card comes from the legends set. Here's a line often attributed to Mahatma Gandhi: Happiness is when what you think, what you say, and what you do are in harmony.
Mahatma Gandhi (1869, 1948) led India's independence movement through non-violent resistance and became a global symbol of truth, simplicity, and service.
Here's a fresh idea from a recent podcast, Joy Lab Podcast. Act consistently with your authentic values and preferences. Create a "values tattoo" that visually captures what matters most.
Your action for today: write three values and choose one action that matches them. Have a great day.

Good morning. Today's card comes from the legends set. Here's a line often attributed to Viktor Frankl: View your life from your funeral, looking back at your life experiences, what have you accomplished? What would you have wanted to accomplish but didn't? What were the happy moments? What were the sad? What would you do again, and what you wouldn't?
Viktor Frankl was an Austrian psychiatrist and Holocaust survivor who developed logotherapy, the idea that people are motivated by meaning rather than pleasure or power alone.
Here's a fresh idea from a recent study. Review past achievements, unfinished goals, regrets, and lessons to create meaning and purpose.
Your action for today: write three accomplishments, three regrets, and one lesson learned. Have a great day.
Good morning. Today's card comes from the legends set. Dalai Lama once said: Happiness is not something ready made. It comes from your own actions.
The Dalai Lama's teaching is that happiness is built through daily choices, mental habits, kindness and compassion, not simply waiting for perfect circumstances.
Here's a fresh idea from a recent podcast, Miracle Morning. Spend five minutes breathing and accepting the day as it is, then write three things you are grateful for.
Your action for today: set a five-minute timer, breathe, then list three gratitudes. Have a great day.
Good morning. Today's card comes from the legends set. Mark Manson once said: Happiness is like being cool - the harder you try the less it's going to happen. So stop trying. Start living.
Mark Manson is a self-help author and blogger known for counterintuitive advice about happiness, values, and living well.
Here's a fresh idea from a recent podcast, Mark Manson. Happiness is a side effect of doing the right things for the right reasons, not a target to chase.
Your action for today: pick one area and stop measuring happiness there for a week. Have a great day.

Good morning. Today's card comes from the legends set. Richard Branson once said: Most people would assume my business success, and the wealth that comes with it, have brought me happiness. But I know I am successful, wealthy, and connected because I am happy.
Branson says happiness, not wealth or status, is how he measures success and what enables it.
Here's a fresh idea from a recent article. Use happiness as your main success measure, not income or status. Treat money as a tool, not the goal.
Your action for today: rate today's happiness and learning from 1, 10. Have a great day.

Good morning. Today's card comes from the legends set. Here's a line often attributed to Zig Ziglar: Happiness is not a destination, it's a journey. Happiness is not tomorrow, it is now. Happiness is what you are, not what you have.
Zig Ziglar was a motivational speaker and author known for practical advice on success, goal-setting, and self-improvement.
Here's a fresh idea from a recent podcast, Harvard Business Review IdeaCast. Treat happiness as a direction you move toward through habits, empathy, and purpose, not a fixed state to reach.
Your action for today: choose one habit that builds purpose and do it today. Have a great day.

Good morning. Today's card comes from the legends set. Here's a line often attributed to Denis Waitley: The biggest challenge in the world is to be yourself... and to be happy with that. Happiness is the ultimate success.
Denis Waitley was a motivational author and speaker known for ideas about self-responsibility, resilience, and happiness.
Here's a fresh idea from a recent podcast, Labels Don't Define Us. Notice when you are performing an identity for others' expectations. Practice one small act of honest self-expression this week.
Your action for today: share one true preference or feeling with someone you trust. Have a great day.

Good morning. Today's card comes from the legends set. James Clear once said: Happiness is simply the ability to not want more; to find gratitude and satisfaction in the moment that you have right now.
James Clear is a writer and habits expert known for Atomic Habits. His happiness advice centers on gratitude, presence, and improving life without abandoning the present.

Here's a fresh idea from a recent podcast, Huberman Lab Essentials. Use a specific memory of genuine thanks, then recall its emotional details for one to five minutes. Story-based gratitude may be more engaging than simply listing items.
Your action for today: write three cues from a meaningful thank-you moment, then revisit them for one minute. Have a great day.

Good morning. Today's card comes from the legends set. Jordan Peterson once said: We are not happy, technically speaking, unless we see ourselves progressing - and the very idea of progression implies value.
Peterson argues that happiness depends on perceiving progress toward valued goals, not merely comfort or pleasure.
Here's a fresh idea from a recent article. Turn friction into progress signals
Your action for today: the Doji. Have a great day.
Good morning. Today's card comes from the legends set. Here's a line often attributed to Jordan Belfort: Whether you say, 'I can' or 'I can't,' you're right either way.
Jordan Belfort is a former stockbroker, author, and motivational speaker known for The Wolf of Wall Street. His work emphasizes belief, self-talk, persistence, and taking action.
Here's a fresh idea from a recent article. Positive mantras paired with action
Your action for today: action turns self-talk into evidence. Have a great day.
Good morning. Today's card comes from the legends set. Steve Jobs once said: If today were the last day of my life, would I want to do what I'm about to do today?
Steve Jobs used this question as a daily test for whether his life and work were aligned with what mattered to him.
Here's a fresh idea from a recent article. Use the question to identify one opportunity or task that conflicts with your purpose. Say no to it to make room for what you love.
Your action for today: name one commitment you could stop or reduce today. Have a great day.
Good morning. Today's card comes from the actors set. Leonardo DiCaprio once said: If you can do what you do best and be happy, you're further along in life than most people.
Leonardo DiCaprio is an actor, producer, and environmental activist who has said happiness and doing what you love matter more than wealth or success.
Here's a fresh idea from a recent article. Identify one activity you are naturally good at and practice it regularly. Building strengths can increase motivation and confidence.
Your action for today: list three things you enjoy and are good at. Have a great day.

Good morning. Today's card comes from the actors set. Here's a line often attributed to Meryl Streep: The formula of happiness and success is just, being actually yourself, in the most vivid possible way you can.
Meryl Streep is an acclaimed American actress known for bringing emotional depth and authenticity to her roles.
Here's a fresh idea from a recent article. Ask whether a change brings you closer to who you want to be or merely closer to approval.
Your action for today: choose one decision today that feels genuinely yours. Have a great day.
Good morning. Today's card comes from the actors set. Johnny Depp once said: Money doesn't buy you happiness, but it buys you a big enough yacht to sail right up to it.
Johnny Depp used the line in a 2009 Vanity Fair interview about his Bahamian island and yacht.
Here's a fresh idea from a recent article. Money can add comfort, but fulfillment comes from inner sources. Build daily practices that support your wellbeing rather than relying on purchases.
Your action for today: write one thing you did today that felt meaningful. Have a great day.
Good morning. Today's card comes from the actors set. Here's a line often attributed to Will Smith: I wake up every morning believing today is going to be better than yesterday.
Will Smith is an actor, rapper, and producer known for optimism, hard work, and personal growth.
Here's a fresh idea from a recent article. Stay ready by treating each morning as a beginner
Your action for today: positive Scope. Have a great day.

Good morning. Today's card comes from the actors set. Here's a line often attributed to Jared Leto: Happiness is like the weather. Sometimes it's rainy, sometimes it's sunny, and you gotta just go through and accept what's there in front of you.
Jared Leto is an actor and musician known for roles in Requiem for a Dream, A History of Violence, and Suicide Squad, and for founding the band 30 Seconds to Mars.
Here's a fresh idea from a recent article. Treat low mood as weather: acknowledge it without judging it, then keep doing one small task.
Your action for today: name your mood, then finish one five-minute task. Have a great day.
Good morning. Today's card comes from the actors set. Robert De Niro once said: Time goes on. So whatever you're going to do, do it. Do it now. Don't wait.
De Niro's reminder to act now comes from a 2009 interview about his long career and changing priorities.
Here's a fresh idea from a recent article. Start a task today even if it is imperfect; progress comes from action, not ideal conditions.
Your action for today: pick one postponed task and do a 10-minute version today. Have a great day.
Good morning. Today's card comes from the actors set. Jennifer Aniston once said: If you're not happy, you can become happy. Happiness is a choice.
Jennifer Aniston, the actress best known for Friends, spoke about choosing happiness and self-awareness in a 2013 Glamour interview.
Here's a fresh idea from a recent article. Spend time identifying who you are and what you genuinely love about yourself. Self-knowledge helps decisions and relationships fall into place.
Your action for today: write three things you love about yourself. Have a great day.
Good morning. Today's card comes from the actors set. Here's a line often attributed to Hugh Jackman: In life you don't regret the things you do, you regret the things you don't do.

Hugh Jackman is an Australian actor, singer, and dancer known for Wolverine, Les Misérables, and The Greatest Showman. His public advice emphasizes taking risks, pursuing what you love, and not giving up dreams.
Here's a fresh idea from a recent article. Plan a small, achievable win before the day starts. Share it with someone who can hold you accountable.
Your action for today: text a friend one goal you will finish today. Have a great day.
Good morning. Today's card comes from the actors set. Keanu Reeves once said: You have to change your life if you're not happy, and wake up if things aren't going the way you want.
Reeves described Henry's Crime as an allegory and fable about changing your life when you are unhappy.

Here's a fresh idea from a recent study. Identify your core values, then turn them into small goals or actions. Research finds acting on values improves well-being more consistently than reflection alone.
Your action for today: pick one value and schedule one action aligned with it. Have a great day.
Good morning. Today's card comes from the actors set. Anthony Hopkins once said: There is no shortcut to happiness, you have to live your life.
Anthony Hopkins, Welsh actor and director, spoke about pursuing acting from a working-class Welsh town and learning to keep moving beyond comfort zones.
Here's a fresh idea from a recent article. Happiness comes from getting up and living, not from waiting for a perfect plan.
Your action for today: do one small thing today that moves you toward a goal. Have a great day.
Good morning. Today's card comes from the singers set. Beyoncé once said: Happiness comes from you. No one else can make you happy. You make you happy.
Beyoncé's 2014 "Yours and Mine" short film reflects on fame, feminism, marriage, loss, and happiness.
Here's a fresh idea from a recent article. Treat happiness as a daily practice of self-compassion rather than something others must provide.
Your action for today: write one kind sentence to yourself today. Have a great day.

Good morning. Today's card comes from the singers set. Here's a line often attributed to Wiz Khalifa: You don't need too many people to be happy; just a few real ones who appreciate you for who you are.
Wiz Khalifa is an American rapper, songwriter, and actor known for "Black and Yellow" and "Rolling Papers."
Here's a fresh idea from a recent article. Prioritize a small circle of people who genuinely appreciate you over a large social network. Authenticity and mutual respect matter more than popularity.
Your action for today: name three people who truly accept you and thank one of them. Have a great day.
Good morning. Today's card comes from the singers set. Here's a line often attributed to Harry Styles: If you're happy doing what you love, nobody can tell you that you're not successful.
Harry Styles redefined success after leaving One Direction, prioritizing authentic, joyful music over external validation.
Here's a fresh idea from a recent podcast, A Bit of Optimism. Trust a decision when your gut, values, and evidence broadly align; use the 80/20/0 rule.
Your action for today: list three reasons for and against a choice, then rate your confidence. Have a great day.
Good morning. Today's card comes from the singers set. Here's a line often attributed to Chris Martin: Life is beautiful in all it's colors, even the darker ones, they're here for a reason.
Chris Martin is the British singer-songwriter and lead vocalist of Coldplay. The card's quote is attributed to him, but its origin is not verified.
Here's a fresh idea from a recent study. Treat a hard day as a challenge to learn from, not a threat to erase. Ask what it is revealing about your values or priorities.
Your action for today: write one sentence about what today taught you. Have a great day.
Good morning. Today's card comes from the singers set. Adam Levine once said: It's much more interesting to embrace who you really are rather than waste energy pretending to be someone else.
Adam Levine is the lead singer and songwriter of Maroon 5, a Los Angeles-born musician who built a career in pop-rock music.
Think about this today: Being yourself.
Your action for today: pick one small step from this card and do it before lunch. Have a great day.
Good morning. Today's card comes from the singers set. Katy Perry once said: I'm happy, I'm in a good place, I'm looking forward to my future.
In July 2012, Perry said this while discussing her next album and refusing to make it entirely about heartbreak.

Here's a fresh idea from a recent article. Turn setbacks into growth by focusing on resilience and optimism. Perry's later work shows how personal struggles can become empowering, forward-looking stories.
Your action for today: write one recent setback and one lesson it taught you. Have a great day.
Good morning. Today's card comes from the singers set. Mika once said: I make mistakes. I say stupid things. I do idiotic things. And, quite frankly, I'm proud of them. Why not make mistakes?
Mika, the British-Lebanese pop singer, made the statement in 2007 after a breakthrough year for his debut album Life in Cartoon Motion.

Here's a fresh idea from a recent podcast, Hidden Brain Media. Aim for small, hypothesis-driven "intelligent failures" that produce useful information. Design a low-risk experiment, learn from the result, and correct course.
Your action for today: try one tiny experiment this week and note what it teaches you. Have a great day.
Good morning. Today's card comes from the singers set. Lizzo once said: If I'm shinin', everybody gonna shine. I was born like this, don't even gotta try.
Lizzo is an American singer, rapper, songwriter, and flutist known for confident, body-positive music and self-acceptance.
Here's a fresh idea from a recent study. Use short self-compassion podcast episodes to treat setbacks as normal, not proof you are inadequate.
Your action for today: listen to one self-compassion episode after a mistake. Have a great day.
Good morning. Today's card comes from the singers set. Here's a line often attributed to Ryan Tedder: I have a theory that you can decide to make whatever day it is a good day.
Ryan Tedder is a singer-songwriter and founding member of OneRepublic. The quote is widely attributed to him, but its original source is not identified.
Here's a fresh idea from a recent study. Use a short daily positive exercise, such as writing about a best possible future self. Repeated practice can improve mood and well-being over time.
Your action for today: spend five minutes writing about a future day you would love. Have a great day.
Good morning. Today's card comes from the singers set. Madonna once said: Happiness lies in your hand.
Madonna is a singer, songwriter, and performer known for self-reliance, reinvention, and taking control of her own life.
Here's a fresh idea from a recent article. Build happiness through tiny daily habits rather than dramatic life changes. Practice three gratitudes each morning and attach them to an existing routine.
Your action for today: after brushing your teeth, name three things you're grateful for. Have a great day.
Good morning. Today's card comes from the movies set. From Forrest Gump, Forrest Gump says: Life is like a box of chocolates. You never know what you are gonna get.
Forrest Gump (1994) is a film about a kind, determined man with an IQ of 75 whose life intersects major American events.
Think about this today: Uncertainty and choice.
Your action for today: pick one small step from this card and do it before lunch. Have a great day.

Good morning. Today's card comes from the movies set. From Rocky Balboa, Rocky Balboa says: It ain't how hard you can hit. It's how hard you can get hit and keep moving forward. It's how much you can take, and keep moving forward. That's how winning is done.
Rocky Balboa is an aging boxer returning from retirement to face a younger opponent. He tells his son that winning comes from enduring setbacks and continuing forward.
Here's a fresh idea from a recent article. Set realistic goals and celebrate each small win to strengthen confidence and momentum.
Your action for today: the Auspicious Advice. Have a great day.
Good morning. Today's card comes from the movies set. Walt Disney once said: The way to get started is to quit talking and begin doing.
Walt Disney's 1957 words were about proving to bankers that his ventures could succeed commercially, not a general life motto.

Here's a fresh idea from a recent podcast, Disney Magical Mindset Podcast. Choose one action you can take today, then repeat it daily for 30 days. Track the visible change instead of waiting to feel ready.
Your action for today: choose one 10-minute action and schedule it for today and the next seven days. Have a great day.
Good morning. Today's card comes from the movies set. From Mission: Impossible – Fallout, August Walker says: Hope is not a strategy.
August Walker is a CIA assassin who is secretly John Lark, the film's main antagonist.

Here's a fresh idea from a recent podcast, The Gregory Vetter Podcast. Keep hope as motivation, but turn it into a realistic plan with preparation for setbacks. Prepare for likely problems rather than relying on a good outcome.
Your action for today: write one goal, its first step, and one likely obstacle. Have a great day.

Good morning. Today's card comes from the movies set. From The Pursuit of Happyness, Chris Gardner says: Don't ever let somebody tell you you can't do something, not even me. Alright? You dream, you gotta protect it. People can't do something themselves, they wanna tell you - you can't do it. If you want something, go get it.
Chris Gardner is a father and aspiring salesman who endures homelessness and hardship while pursuing a better life for his son.
Here's a fresh idea from a recent article. When someone says you can't do it, write one small next step toward your goal instead of arguing.
Your action for today: choose one 15-minute action toward a goal you want. Have a great day.
Good morning. Today's card comes from the movies set. From Winnie the Pooh, Piglet says: The things that make me different are the things that make me.
Piglet is a small, anxious but loyal character from A. A.
Here's a fresh idea from a recent video. Treat awkwardness and quirks as safe, valued parts of identity. Practice grace when you or others feel "weird."
Your action for today: say "I'm glad you're you" to someone. Have a great day.
Good morning. Today's card comes from the movies set. Here's a line often attributed to Jack Sparrow: The problem is not the problem. The problem is your attitude about the problem.
Captain Jack Sparrow is the witty, rum-loving pirate from Pirates of the Caribbean: The Curse of the Black Pearl (2003), played by Johnny Depp.
Here's a fresh idea from a recent podcast, Up and Not Crying. Separate the facts from your thoughts, feelings, and actions, then focus only on what you can control.
Your action for today: next time stress hits, ask: "What can I actually do?". Have a great day.
Good morning. Today's card comes from the movies set. From DuckTales the Movie, Donald Duck says: Happiness is the richest thing we will ever own.
Donald Duck, the short-tempered Disney duck, delivers this line in the 1990 DuckTales film.
Here's a fresh idea from a recent article. True wealth includes calm, genuine laughter, healthy relationships, and peace of mind, not only money or status. Protect those things when making choices.
Your action for today: list three non-material things you are grateful for today. Have a great day.

Good morning. Today's card comes from the movies set. From Harry Potter and the Prisoner of Azkaban, Albus Dumbledore says: Happiness can be found even in the darkest of times, if one only remembers to turn on the light.
Dumbledore says it during his start-of-year address after Dementors arrive at Hogwarts, warning students about their despair-draining power.
Here's a fresh idea from a recent podcast, Life Notes From Chair 17. Protect your attention and stay connected to people and things that bring joy during uncertain times.
Your action for today: turn off doom scrolling and text one supportive friend. Have a great day.
